header.title: A hanok space where traditional furniture of the Joseon dynasty comes alive

hamstay_section.hanok_description:
LEE SSI HAM | To honor the craftsmanship of the late master Lee Sung-Goo (1927–2000), who devoted himself to carrying on Korea’s Joseon-era tradition of wooden furniture, HAM Hanok Stay is a place where you can stay together with his works.
Stay in a cultural space where you can experience both an authentic Bukchon hanok and Joseon wooden furniture in one place.

Accommodation
An entire hanok house located in Bukchon — “HAM Hanok Stay”.

A family-oriented whole hanok with a cozy courtyard, suitable for 3 adults or 2 adults + 2 children. Please note in advance that two adults in the sarang room may feel it a little compact depending on preference.

The ondol stone meets the sky, and the stone embankment seen through the full-height glass gives a classical mood.

For 2 guests – a queen-size bedding set is provided in the main room.
(If you wish to sleep separately, please let us know in advance.)

For 3–4 guests – queen-size bedding sets are provided in both the main room and the sarang room.

Each room has its own toilet/shower.

The day before check-in, we send a guide manual including the door code by message; in-person check-in is also available.

Guest access / Facilities
📌 Spaces
Toenmaru & small courtyard, kitchen, living room, main room, bathroom 1, sarang room, bathroom 2

📌 Facilities
[Bathroom]
Towels / Dyson hair dryer
Bamboo toothbrush / toothpaste / shampoo, conditioner, body wash / bidet (installed in the sarang room)

[Main & Sarang rooms]
Queen-size bedding

[Living room]
4 floor cushions, Wi-Fi, towel basket

[Kitchen]
Ice purifier
Refrigerator
Microwave
Coffee machine / capsules
Single-burner induction / tableware / basic cookware
First-aid kit
Marshall Bluetooth speaker

[Small courtyard]
Camping table, 2 camping chairs

* Free laundry service for stays of 5 nights or more.
* ❌ Please do not move the furniture without permission. ❌ The wooden furniture is delicate and may be damaged. As they are precious assets of our hanok, please handle with care. If damage occurs, we may have to take firm action to recover costs. Don’t hesitate to ask anything, even small questions.

Other notes
🔒 Exhibited works are highly valuable cultural assets. Please view any pieces with covers with your eyes only. We kindly ask you to treat everything with care during your stay. Any damage, removal, or loss of items and facilities, or irreparable contamination of bedding, will incur compensation.
